dialect.detail: Classic IBM mainframe-style COBOL with RECORDING MODE, ACCEPT FROM DATE (2-digit year), GOBACK, and carriage-control conventions. No EXEC SQL/CICS. Likely compiled under IBM Enterprise COBOL or compatible.
evidence: ACCEPT TODAYS-DATE FROM DATE (2-digit year YY)

purpose.domain_detail: COVID-19 USA historical data reporting — reads a CSV file of US COVID-19 statistics (cases, hospitalizations, ICU, ventilator, deaths) and produces a printed bar-graph report showing death-rate percentage over time.
purpose.summary: CBLGRPH reads a comma-delimited USA COVID-19 historical data file (USAHIST), computes the death rate as a percentage of positive cases, and prints a character-based horizontal bar graph on a print file. Each record produces one line with a '*' plotted at the computed percentage position along a 110-character graph axis.

notable_features: UNSTRING with comma delimiter to parse CSV input
Character-based horizontal bar graph using OCCURS 110 TIMES array
ACCEPT FROM DATE for today's date (2-digit year)
Carriage-control fields (TOP-OF-PAGE, SINGLE-SPACE, DOUBLE-SPACE, TRIPLE-SPACE, OVERPRINT)
RECORDING MODE F on both files
Commented-out FD record layout replaced by UNSTRING parsing
Error line for values exceeding 10% threshold
Page heading with ruler line showing percentage scale 0-100
verdict.notes: The 2-digit year from ACCEPT FROM DATE is a minor Y2K-era artifact. The commented-out FD record layout suggests iterative development. The program is self-contained with no COPY or CALL statements. Domain is clearly COVID-19 data (field names: UHR-CASE-POSITIVE, UHR-DEATH, UHR-ICU, UHR-VENT, etc.), suggesting a personal or educational project written during the pandemic era.
